NASA's Artemis II crew safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT), concluding a historic 10-day mission around the moon. The four astronauts (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) returned in the Orion capsule, marking the first crewed deep-space return in over 50 years. Artemis II Splashdown Details (April 10, 2026) Location: Pacific Ocean, off the coast of San Diego, California. Time: 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT). Visibility: A potential sonic boom may have been heard across Southern California. Mission Goal: To verify the Orion spacecraft and SLS rocket systems for future lunar missions. Other Rocket Activity (April 10-11, 2026) A SpaceX Falcon 9 launch was scheduled for late Friday night (April 10) from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, separate from the NASA mission. How to Watch Replays NASA Live Stream: Coverage of the splashdown and recovery is available via NASA's official YouTube channel. News Coverage: Major news outlets covered the reentry live.
